end.summary:
Zoya described how the East India Company changed from trading to ruling.
They explained the use of forts, armies, battles, alliances/protection payments and Bengal’s revenue rights.
They connected the 1765 revenue rights to funding a larger army and further expansion.
They described heavy taxation, factory closures, and causes of the 1857 revolt, including cartridges and punishment.
Teach-back was not passed; two unaided attempts on Company methods were correct.
end.parentNote: Zoya practised explaining how the Company gained power through forts, armies, battles, alliances and revenue rights. Their explanation successfully linked the 1765 tax-collection right to Company income, army expansion and further control. They also mixed up some details while describing the 1857 revolt, including the sequence and place of early events; this was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Zoya to make a five-step timeline from trade to Company rule, including 1765 and 1857.
